### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. Bartsocas-Papas syndrome 2  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.730)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:1974)

**Proposed mechanism:** CHUK (HGNC:1974) —DISRUPTS→ NF-kappa B signaling pathway (KEGG:hsa04064); NF-kappa B signaling pathway (KEGG:hsa04064) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal inflammatory response (HP:0011221); NF-kappa B signaling pathway (KEGG:hsa04064) —LEADS_TO→ Skeletal dysplasia (HP:0002713). Loss-of-function mutations in CHUK disrupt the NF-kappa B signaling pathway. Dysregulation of this pathway leads to abnormal inflammatory responses and skeletal dysplasia, contributing to the phenotypes of both MONDO:0013334 and Bartsocas-Papas syndrome 2.

**How to falsify it:** The discovery of pathogenic variants in CHUK in individuals with MONDO:0013334 or Bartsocas-Papas syndrome 2 that result in a gain-of-function mechanism would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: Exome sequencing of a large cohort of patients with either disease reveals no pathogenic variants in CHUK.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of CHUK in regulating NF-kappa B signaling could lead to therapeutic strategies targeting this pathway for both conditions.
